plain_what: How a finished model runs on an ordinary laptop or in a browser using only whole numbers, adds, shifts and table look-ups, with no floating-point maths and no multiply instruction. A trained model is exported to a compact file, and an audit counts machine instructions to prove no multiply sneaks in.
how_it_works: Training is done offline in float. For serving, the weights are exported into a UORLUT01 container: 4-bit weights in groups of 32, each group with a one-byte scale (4-bit mantissa, 4-bit exponent), plus integer tables for the few nonlinear steps (square root, decay rates, SiLU, arcosh, exp). The D11 engine then computes every token with integers only. A projection y = W x is done by building, for each activation, a 16-entry table of its multiples, using each weight's 4-bit code as an index into that table, and applying group scales by shifts and adds, with four rows blocked to reuse the table. A product of two runtime values (a score, a gate, a value mix) uses a quarter-square table, (a+b)^2/4 - (a-b)^2/4 from a lookup, or shift-add; normalization uses an integer square root or table; sampling is integer min-p. The state of a conversation is saved and restored byte-exactly (UR4SESS1). The contract has five rules: no float and no libm (R1), no multiply or divide instruction (R2), dense per-token access to a learned store is interim, not the end state (R3, D5), no transformer backbone (R4), and energy is claimed only when measured (R5). Compliance is checked by static disassembly of the release binary, counting multiply, divide and float instructions over the serving symbols, native and WebAssembly.
geometry: Exact finite tables rather than approximate maths: the binary icosahedral group (2I, 120 elements) Cayley table of about 14 KiB, signed permutations, Z[phi] shift-add products, a 1,025-entry arcosh table for Lorentz read scores, icosian-pair weights with a 2-bit mantissa, and the Q30 Hopf S3-to-S2 observation. The current integer crate selects typed H4 geometry and checked scalar integer arithmetic (native_geometry.rs) for the discrete model's own export.

status_reason: ACTIVE as the end-of-pipeline contract (M4 #2032): D37 makes the integer export the boundary, and native (44 symbol ranges) and WebAssembly (7/7) zero-mul audits are green (docs/integration/project-track.md M4). No lawful trained model has been exported yet; the D10 LUT engines are excluded (docs/history/d29-excluded-lut-2026-10-13).
reopen_conditions: Sub-part only: the D10 LUT engine and uor-r4-simd stay frozen non-mission comparators; they return only if an owner decision restores a multiplier-allowing serving tier (D11 item 2 withdrew it).
Sub-part only: serving of product-key memory needs an integer kernel; export_stack refuses it today (docs/labs/native-address-port-2026-10-11/README.md).

rule_compat.D11: This is D11. Bit-exact against its float reference on every windowed check (d11 minus d10 NLL 0.0, max logit difference 0), zero multiply, divide and float instructions across audited symbols. Residual gap: dense per-token weight access (about 30.2M parameters read per token for the 29M stack) is interim and D5-b non-compliant; D5-a residency is unmeasured until hardware counters exist (D38).
rule_compat.D23: Partly non-compliant today. Schemas /1 and /2 serve softmax attention reads through exp-table masses, which D29 names; Kimi's 12 October review records 'softmax at runtime: yes'. Schema /3 serves softmax-free flock rank reads, but the trained softmax-free arms missed the 0.01 BPB bar (docs/labs/softmax-free-read-2026-10-10/README.md).
rule_compat.D30: Table GEMV streams every weight each token, which D5 calls a dense multiply in disguise; D25 closed dense low-bit maps as a stepping stone. The lawful target is selected addressed reads and exact geometry tables, not these kernels. Engines containing hidden dense contractions were quarantined in D29 (docs/labs/d29-module-split-2026-10-13/README.md).
rule_compat.D32_D37: D37 item 3: float training is legal offline; the export is the integer boundary and every candidate must report its export gap on the same evaluator. Precedent gaps: 0.00883 to 0.0194 BPB (19.9M stack), 0.0106 nats after QAT, up to 0.036 nats round-to-nearest (7M stack); no discrete-path export exists yet.

experiments.configuration: Source-free integer n-gram table (SFTBL001) on held-out lexical targets, no teacher at run time
experiments.result: Integer lookup predicts held-out lexical targets well above a unigram; a statistical lexical result, not semantic.

experiments.configuration: Learned attention, recurrence and transport of two accepted 1.68M learned-code parents executed with integer arithmetic and offline-compiled tables
experiments.result: Both arms met the unchanged numerical bounds and kept every previously correct source answer; language quality remains unproven.
experiments.numbers: Q48 probabilities sum exactly to 2^48; context 256/256/256 with all 255 previous occurrences visible

experiments.configuration: Standalone uor-r4-integer library and CLI over the same two bundles, independent saved-data comparison
experiments.result: Exact reproduction of saved distributions and a measured speedup after one arithmetic fix; language quality unchanged.
experiments.numbers: all 4,096 Q48 distribution hashes and greedy predictions match; about 4.5-6.6x faster after one measured fix

experiments.configuration: Jointly learned choice between the two legal neighbouring 4-bit codes of each coordinate, quaternion and Householder-pair arms
experiments.result: Both arms passed all five retention gates but stay above the continuous references; engineering continuation only.
experiments.numbers: hard minus continuous +0.0237 (quaternion) and +0.0465 (Householder pair) nats vs gate 0.05; hard parents were 2.1503 and 2.1479

experiments.configuration: Four-bit multiplicative / 16-bit additive quantization-aware continuation of the joint recurrent learner; projected-shadow variant in projected-recurrent-result-2026-09-25.md
experiments.result: Both QAT recipes rejected: packed arms exceeded the retention allowance; the ordinary arm also fell into a period-two cycle.
experiments.numbers: packed minus continuous +0.059 (quaternion) / +0.080 (Householder) nats; projected +0.060 / +0.084; gate +0.05

experiments.configuration: Shared packed signed4 coefficient storage against the unpacked baseline on two retained width-256 models, 16 processes
experiments.result: All frozen replay, generation and chat outputs identical while retained coefficient bytes fell; dense access remains.
experiments.numbers: 8/8 baseline-candidate pairs match; coefficient bytes down 87%

experiments.configuration: First measured whole-system marginal energy of the per-product-table integer path against its float parent on the owner's laptop
experiments.result: Table emulation of every product cost more energy and time than float; recorded as FAILED on energy. Power counters were unavailable on this OS version.
experiments.numbers: 0.00413 J/token vs 0.00096 for the float parent (about 4.3x worse), about 2.6x slower

experiments.configuration: Cycle-4 7.15M stack exported to the D10/D11 interim format (4-bit groups of 32), evaluation only, 131,072 targets
experiments.result: Export gap misses the 0.02-nat fidelity gate with either quantizer; integer arithmetic costs nothing measurable, the whole gap is weight representation, and the output head is the largest share.
experiments.numbers: round-to-nearest +0.0362 nats, GPTQ +0.0257 nats vs gate 0.02; snapping transport quaternions to the nearest icosian +0.026

experiments.configuration: Float-reference codec arms (round-to-nearest, online Hadamard + grouped 4-bit, Hadamard + single-shell E8) and D11 engine versus NEON reference
experiments.result: No codec arm meets the 0.02-nat gate at 4.25 bits per weight; the D11 engine is bit-identical to the NEON reference at measured cost.
experiments.numbers: float 1.998113; RTN +0.036230; Hadamard+G4 +0.027007; E8 ~2 bpw +2.4235; 184.58 tok/s on 1 thread; energy figures unvalidated (capture truncated at the 64 KiB pipe limit)

experiments.result: Lower development loss but fewer memory-relation answers than nearest rounding: fails the pre-registered retention rule; kept as a negative candidate.

experiments.result: The earlier quoted gap mixed different window counts; on identical positions the engine is exact and the gap is weight quantization.

never_tested: Serving a lawful discrete or float-rung0 model through D11: no such artifact has been exported yet, so the export gap of the current model path is unmeasured.
Hardware-counter measurement of DRAM bytes per token (D5-a residency) and selected-parameter access (D5-b): M5 has not run.

Whole-system energy per token with a validated sampler: the only figures (5.7 and 21.0 mJ/token) came from a truncated capture and are unvalidated; the 4.3x-worse result is from the earlier per-product emulation.
Integer serving of a product-key or addressed memory read (the kernel is not built).
A real serving comparison with the SIMD kernels actually on the hot path.
Free-running generation rate: 184.58 tok/s was input-driven forward throughput, not autoregressive decode.
failed_only_on_configuration: Per-product table emulation was 4.3x worse on energy (docs/history/.../1449-...md): it replaced every multiply with a table read on a dense model, a property of that dense configuration, not of exact table serving of selected geometry.
Hadamard + E8 and QAT recipes missing the 0.02-nat export gate: they concern how a dense float stack was rounded, not whether the integer boundary can hold a model.
The softmax-free read arms (+0.0172 BPB or worse) used host-side rank tables on a stack trained with a softmax control; they say nothing about reads built from the start without softmax.
Served 1.20-1.24 BPB vs 0.90 target: attributed by the record to the float model, not the engine (bit-exact).
open_questions: What is the export gap of a discrete or lawful float model through the D11 container, and does UORLUT01 need a new schema for table-native models rather than 4-bit dense groups?
How much of the 30.2M parameters touched per token can selected addressed reads remove before tokens/s moves, given MACs were not time (product-key memory was slower on the float harness)?
Is D5-a residency (cache-resident artifact) enough for the target model size, or does D5-b sparsity bind?
Should the Python audit scripts be ported to Rust (D27/D30) and run in CI? CUDA and the wasm audit are not built in CI today.

figure_ideas: A single dot product with no multiply: one activation, a 16-slot row of its multiples built once, three 4-bit weight codes lighting the slots they select, a shift for the group scale, and a running sum. A counter beside it reads 'multiply instructions: 0'.

Float versus integer on the same 64 windows: logits plotted against each other sitting exactly on the diagonal (max difference 0), then a separate bar showing the real cost, weight rounding (0.0088 to 0.0194 BPB), so a reader sees the engine is exact and the loss is in the weights.
The audit strip: a row of 44 coloured symbol ranges from the release binary, each tagged with counts of multiply, divide and float instructions, all green, beside the seven WebAssembly symbols.
